requiredAssumptions.description: The request explicitly describes a univariate polynomial representation or algorithm.
The request explicitly constrains coefficients or roots to integers.
The request calls for exact construction, expansion, integer-root checking, or zero verification.

contraindications.description: Reject authentication factor, multi-factor authentication, and identity factor uses.
Reject business, risk, human, market, scaling, and other non-polynomial factors.
Reject generic factor language without an explicit polynomial coding context.
Reject floating-point or approximate root-finding when exact integer polynomial semantics are not explicit.

computationalFormulation: Represent a univariate integer polynomial by coefficients in a declared order. Construct factors by coefficient convolution, expand them deterministically, evaluate candidate integer roots with exact arithmetic, and accept a root only when exact evaluation equals zero.
implementationPatterns: Declare coefficient order and normalize trailing zero coefficients without changing the represented polynomial.
Expand products by exact coefficient convolution and accumulate in an overflow-safe integer representation.
Generate bounded integer-root candidates only from the rational-root constraints applicable to the nonzero constant and leading coefficients.
Verify every returned factorization by re-expansion and every returned root by exact zero evaluation.

verification.strategy: Independently convolve returned integer-coefficient factors and compare every normalized coefficient with the input polynomial; independently evaluate each claimed integer root and require exact zero.

risks.complexity: Naive convolution is O(d1*d2), evaluation by Horner's method is O(d), and exhaustive integer-root enumeration can be dominated by divisor generation; all candidate bounds must remain finite.
risks.numerical: Fixed-width coefficient overflow, coefficient-order confusion, duplicate roots, zero-polynomial ambiguity, and approximate equality can create false factorizations.

truthBoundary: This is a declared coding-transfer hypothesis and deterministic qualification surface. Mathematical mastery, profile validity, transfer qualification, live activation, and empirical coding benefit are separate claims; this profile is not checked in as qualified.
